original: Baloo looked up to see where the voice came from, and there was Rann the Kite, sweeping down with the sun shining on the upturned flanges of his wings. It was near Rann’s bedtime, but he had ranged all over the jungle looking for the Bear and had missed him in the thick foliage.
danish: Baloo løftede blikket mod stemmen. Glenten Rann svævede ned, og solen skinnede på hans opadbøjede vingekanter. Det var næsten hans sengetid, men han havde søgt over hele junglen efter Bjørnen uden at få øje på ham under det tætte løv.

original: Limmershin gave a long list of them, for he said that Kotick spent five seasons exploring, with a four months’ rest each year at Novastoshnah, when the holluschickie used to make fun of him and his imaginary islands. He went to the Gallapagos, a horrid dry place on the Equator, where he was nearly baked to death; he went to the Georgia Islands, the Orkneys, Emerald Island, Little Nightingale Island, Gough’s Island, Bouvet’s Island, the Crossets, and even to a little speck of an island south of the Cape of Good Hope. But everywhere the People of the Sea told him the same things. Seals had come to those islands once upon a time, but men had killed them all off. Even when he swam thousands of miles out of the Pacific and got to a place called Cape Corrientes (that was when he was coming back from Gough’s Island), he found a few hundred mangy seals on a rock and they told him that men came there too.
danish: Limmershin nævnte mange øer. Kotick ledte i fem sæsoner, sagde han, og hvilede hvert år fire måneder ved Novastoshnah, mens holluschickie gjorde nar af hans indbildte tilflugtssteder. På Galápagos, et frygteligt tørt sted ved Ækvator, blev han næsten stegt levende. Han besøgte Sydgeorgien og naboøerne, Sydorkneyøerne, Smaragdøen, Lille Nattergaleø, Goughøen, Bouvetøen, Crozetøerne og endda en lille ø syd for Kap det Gode Håb. På hvert af disse steder talte han med Havets Folk, og overalt fik han det samme nedslående svar: Sæler var engang kommet dertil, men mænd havde dræbt dem alle. På vej hjem fra Goughøen svømmede han tusinder af engelske mil bort fra Stillehavet til Kap Corrientes. Selv dér trængtes nogle hundrede skabede sæler på en klippe og fortalte ham, at mænd kom forbi.

original: Then Rikki-tikki went out into the garden to see what was to be seen. It was a large garden, only half cultivated, with bushes, as big as summer-houses, of Marshal Niel roses, lime and orange trees, clumps of bamboos, and thickets of high grass. Rikki-tikki licked his lips. “This is a splendid hunting-ground,” he said, and his tail grew bottle-brushy at the thought of it, and he scuttled up and down the garden, snuffing here and there till he heard very sorrowful voices in a thorn-bush.
danish: Bagefter udforskede han haven. Den var stor, men kun halvdelen var dyrket. Der var Marshal Niel-rosenbuske, store som lysthuse, lime- og appelsintræer, bambusklynger og krat af højt græs. Rikki-tikki slikkede sig om munden. »Sikke et dejligt jagtområde,« sagde han, og halen svulmede op som en flaskebørste. Han fór rundt og snusede overalt, indtil han hørte sørgmodige stemmer fra en tornebusk.

original: If you read the old books of natural history, you will find they say that when the mongoose fights the snake and happens to get bitten, he runs off and eats some herb that cures him. That is not true. The victory is only a matter of quickness of eye and quickness of foot--snake’s blow against mongoose’s jump--and as no eye can follow the motion of a snake’s head when it strikes, this makes things much more wonderful than any magic herb. Rikki-tikki knew he was a young mongoose, and it made him all the more pleased to think that he had managed to escape a blow from behind. It gave him confidence in himself, and when Teddy came running down the path, Rikki-tikki was ready to be petted.
danish: Gamle bøger om naturen påstår, at en mangust, der bliver bidt i kamp, løber hen og finder en urt, som helbreder ham. Det passer ikke. Sejren kommer af skarpe øjne og hurtige fødder: mangustens spring mod slangens hug. Intet menneskeøje kan følge hovedet på en slange, der hugger, og det gør bedriften mere vidunderlig end nogen magisk plante. Rikki-tikki vidste, at han var ung, og han var ekstra glad for at have undgået et angreb bagfra. Det gav ham selvtillid. Da Teddy kom løbende ned ad stien, var han helt klar til at blive kælet for.

original: Then the elephants were chained by their hind legs to their big stumps of pickets, and extra ropes were fitted to the new elephants, and the fodder was piled before them, and the hill drivers went back to Petersen Sahib through the afternoon light, telling the plains drivers to be extra careful that night, and laughing when the plains drivers asked the reason.
danish: De lænkede elefanternes bagben til tunge pæle, lagde ekstra reb om de nye dyr og stablede foder op foran dem. I eftermiddagslyset vendte bjergmahouterne tilbage til Petersen Sahib. De bad sletternes mahouter være særligt på vagt den nat, og de lo, hver gang nogen spurgte hvorfor.

original: At last Kala Nag stood still between two tree-trunks at the very top of the hill. They were part of a circle of trees that grew round an irregular space of some three or four acres, and in all that space, as Little Toomai could see, the ground had been trampled down as hard as a brick floor. Some trees grew in the center of the clearing, but their bark was rubbed away, and the white wood beneath showed all shiny and polished in the patches of moonlight. There were creepers hanging from the upper branches, and the bells of the flowers of the creepers, great waxy white things like convolvuluses, hung down fast asleep. But within the limits of the clearing there was not a single blade of green--nothing but the trampled earth.
danish: På toppen af bakken standsede Kala Nag mellem to stammer i en ring af træer, der omgav en ujævn lysning på tre eller fire acre (et par fodboldbaner). Overalt derinde var jorden trampet så hård som et gulv af mursten. Et par træer stod midt i lysningen med barken gnedet af, så det hvide træ lyste blankt og poleret i pletterne af måneskin. Slyngplanter hang ned fra de øverste grene. Deres store, voksagtige hvide klokker, der lignede snerleblomster, hang og sov. Men inden for lysningens grænser var der ikke ét grønt strå — kun den nedtrampede jord.

original: Still lying down, Little Toomai looked down upon scores and scores of broad backs, and wagging ears, and tossing trunks, and little rolling eyes. He heard the click of tusks as they crossed other tusks by accident, and the dry rustle of trunks twined together, and the chafing of enormous sides and shoulders in the crowd, and the incessant flick and hissh of the great tails. Then a cloud came over the moon, and he sat in black darkness. But the quiet, steady hustling and pushing and gurgling went on just the same. He knew that there were elephants all round Kala Nag, and that there was no chance of backing him out of the assembly; so he set his teeth and shivered. In a Keddah at least there was torchlight and shouting, but here he was all alone in the dark, and once a trunk came up and touched him on the knee.
danish: Toomai lå fladt ned og så ud over snesevis af brede rygge, baskende ører, svingende snabler og rullende små øjne. Stødtænder klikkede, når de tilfældigt krydsede hinanden; sammenslyngede snabler raslede tørt. Enorme skuldre og sider gned mod hinanden, og store haler piskede og hvislede uafbrudt. En sky dækkede månen, og han blev efterladt i sort mørke. Alligevel fortsatte den stille, jævne skubben, puffen og gurglen som før. Elefanter omgav Kala Nag; det var umuligt at bakke ud. Drengen bed tænderne sammen og rystede. I en keddah var der i det mindste råbende mænd og fakkelskær. Her lå han alene i mørket. Én gang kom en snabel op og rørte ved hans knæ.
